title: BVA Decision 25000006: The legacy appeal is dismissed
text:
Citation Nr: 25000006
Decision Date: 01/02/25	Archive Date: 01/02/25

DOCKET NO. 15-41 160A
DATE: January 2, 2025

ORDER

The legacy appeal is dismissed.

FINDING OF FACT

In April 2024, the Veteran died while this appeal was pending before the Board of Veterans' Appeals (Board).

CONCLUSION OF LAW

Due to the death of the Veteran, the criteria for the dismissal of this appeal have been met. 38 U.S.C. § 7104; 38 C.F.R. § 20.1302.

REASONS AND BASES FOR FINDING AND CONCLUSION

The Veteran served honorably in the Army from November 1968 to August 1971.

These matters come before the Board of Veterans' Appeals (Board) on appeal from an October 2012 rating decision by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Regional Office (RO) and were previously remanded by the Board in June 2020.  

In February 2020, the Veteran testified at a Board hearing before the undersigned. 

In July 2023, the Board issued a decision which the Veteran subsequently appealed to the United States Court of Appeals for Veteran's Claims (the Court).

Unfortunately, in April 2024, the Veteran died.  

The Board acknowledges that in May 2024, the Veteran's representative submitted a motion to withdraw from representation in this matter. Considering the contents of this motion, the Board finds that the requirements of a withdrawal of representation contained in 38 C.F.R. § 20.6 have not been met and to ensure due process, the representative of record is retained for the purpose of this dismissal.  

In September 2024, the Court issued a decision vacating the appealed Board decision and dismissing the appeal unless there has been a request for substitution in the appeal before the Court. Accordingly, the Court dismissed the appeal for lack of jurisdiction. 

Unfortunately, as the Veteran died during the pendency of the appeal, as a matter of law, the Board cannot issue a decision on the underlying claims at this time and must dismiss this appeal. 38 C.F.R. § 20.1302(a).

The Board's dismissal does not affect the right of an eligible person to take the Veteran's place to continue the appeal on the pending claims. This process, known as substitution, must be requested within one year of the Veteran's death. 38 C.F.R. § 3.1010(a), (b). Individuals who may be eligible for substitution include the Veteran's surviving spouse, dependent children, dependent parents, and those who bore the expenses of last sickness or burial. 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.1000(a), 3.1010(a).

In this case, no one has requested to substitute for the Veteran. Any person who would like to request substitution must submit a VA Form 21P-0847, "Request for Substitution of Claimant Upon Death of Claimant." The form and filing instructions are available online at https://www.va.gov/find-forms/. If the AOJ receives a request for substitution within one year of the Veteran's death and then grants the request, this dismissed appeal will resume its place on the Board's docket. 38 C.F.R. § 20.1302(a).

Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed.

 

 

Nathaniel Doan

Veterans Law Judge

Board of Veterans' Appeals

Attorney for the Board	N. M. Younan

The Board's decision in this case is binding only with respect to the instant matter decided. This decision is not precedential and does not establish VA policies or interpretations of general applicability. 38 C.F.R. § 20.1303.
